image.alt: Picture of the new information board

body.text: **Information board appears at waterfall claiming it was man-made all along, though nobody can account for who installed the board.**

*A board has appeared at the Ashgrove waterfall crediting its construction to a plumbing squadron nobody can find, drawing water from a mountain that appears on no map. The council says the signage was always part of the plan. Fish News does not.*

In a development that has done nothing whatsoever to settle the matter, a large wooden information board has appeared beside the waterfall at the former Ashgrove Long Stay Car Park, announcing the structure as "The first ever English Artificial water fall." Fish News notes that the board was not present on Thursday, and that the hillside it is mounted in was not present on Tuesday.

The board states that the waterfall was constructed to "boost the eco-system," delivering "nuitriance and enviromental flow" to land and sea species alike. Fish News has reproduced the spelling exactly, as we believe it to be relevant. We are asked to accept that a body which files its own minutes in triplicate produced this board, and that it did so before the hill existed.

The water, according to the board, is pumped through pipes inside Mount Cranwell and administrated by No. 47 Plumbing Squadron. Fish News has been unable to locate Mount Cranwell on any Ordnance Survey map printed before this month, and has found no record of Plumbing Squadrons one through forty-six. The council has not explained the gap.

A council spokesperson, reached by telephone, said the board had been "part of the plan for some time" and declined to say which plan, or whose. Pressed on the planning application, the spokesperson referred us to the public register. The public register contains no such application. Pressed again, the spokesperson referred us to the board.
Asked whether a car park had been demolished to accommodate the project, the spokesperson said that parking enforcement remained fully operational, which Fish News observes is not a denial.

An individual described to us only as "a man in overalls with a No. 47 shoulder patch" was found adjusting nothing in particular near the plunge pool. Asked where the pipes ran to, he said the waterfall was "performing within tolerance" and asked whether we had a permit to be standing there.

Chunce Whatney, reporting from the treeline, was unmoved. "I helped survey the aqueduct at Segovia. I have carried mortar for men who are now dust. Do not show me a painted board and tell me about plumbing."

Fish News has submitted a freedom of information request regarding the procurement of the board, its installation, and the identity of whoever signed the invoice. We were informed the request was received. We were not informed by whom.
This outlet takes no position on what is happening at Ashgrove. We simply decline to take the council's.
